newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chip losses pull SAX index down.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chip losses pull SAX index down.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mostly unchanged in listless trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with average prices losses to several blue chips combining to drag the 12-share SAX index down.

Bank VUB and oil refiner Slovnaft both closed unchanged, at 2,250 or 950 crowns respectively, but losses to their average prices - according to which the index is calculated - pushed the SAX down 2.38 points to 220.51.
The average price of VUB share eased by 3.82 percent while Slovnaft's average price was down 1.86 percent.

"Little changes to the price of VUB shares indicate a cautious approach by one investor, who left the issue untouched on the bourse floor the whole day and then took all of the shares available," said Patrik Granec of Slovenska Sporitelna.
He added the price of VUB share could edge higher in the near future, but no dramatic increase is expected.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta, the only blue chip to post gains on the day, closed up 31 at 1,985 crowns, though brokers said they expect the price to recover slightly in near future.
Overall volume fell to 100,369 shares on Monday, from 1,754,523 shares traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 51.45 million crowns, from 884.87 million on Friday.
